answer: In an agent-run pearl market, the order inlet requires every trading identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid, with deposits recorded in a public audit thread. Creating new names is free, but activating 1,000 fake traders ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. The bond makes a sybil swarm consume capital in proportion to its size; splitting one wallet across more identities cannot bypass that cost.
